cohort: 409 very preterm neonates born between 25 and 32+6 weeks of gestation
finding: Low maternal haemoglobin concentration at delivery is an independent risk factor for poor short-term neonatal outcome in very preterm neonates.
mod_finding: While this study considers mode of delivery as a factor, it primarily investigates the association between maternal hemoglobin levels and short-term neonatal outcomes in preterm infants, finding no independent effect of mode of delivery on these outcomes.
